slides.title: Need a *new field* in VBAK?
slides.voiceover: Stop editing VBAK: use these two structures. Last time we learned cardinality. Now, include and append structures.
slides.spoken: Stop editing VBAK: use these two structures. Last time we learned cardinality. Now, include and append structures.

slides.label: REUSE
slides.heading: One structure, *many tables*
slides.voiceover: Why? Many tables need the same address fields. Put them in a structure: fields that hold no data. Each table includes it. Change it once, every table gets it.
slides.spoken: Why? Many tables need the same address fields. Put them in a structure: fields that hold no data. Each table includes it. Change it once, every table gets it.

slides.heading: Type *.INCLUDE* in Fields
slides.note: its fields appear in the table
slides.voiceover: In SE11, open your table's Fields tab. In a new row, type dot INCLUDE as the field name. Enter ZS_ADDRESS as the data element. Activate.
slides.spoken: In SE11, open your table's Fields tab. In a new row, type .INCLUDE as the field name. Enter ZS_ADDRESS as the data element. Activate.

slides.label: THE PROBLEM
slides.heading: VBAK is *SAP's* table
slides.voiceover: But VBAK belongs to SAP. Editing it is a modification. So add an append structure: your structure, attached to one SAP table. Its fields land at the end. VBAK stays untouched.
slides.spoken: But VBAK belongs to SAP. Editing it is a modification. So add an append structure: your structure, attached to one SAP table. Its fields land at the end. VBAK stays untouched.

slides.heading: Click *Append Structure*
slides.voiceover: Display VBAK in SE11 and click Append Structure. Name it ZAVBAK. Add the field ZZPRIORITY with its data element. Then activate.
slides.spoken: Display VBAK in SE11 and click Append Structure. Name it ZAVBAK. Add the field ZZPRIORITY with its data element. Then activate.

slides.label: COMMON MISTAKE
slides.heading: Field names *without ZZ*

bad.title: PRIORITY
bad.sub: SAP may ship the same name later

slides.voiceover: Common mistake: naming the field just PRIORITY. SAP could ship that exact name in a later upgrade. Then it clashes. Use the Z Z prefix.
slides.spoken: Common mistake: naming the field just PRIORITY. SAP could ship that exact name in a later upgrade. Then it clashes. Use the ZZ prefix.

slides.label: REMEMBER
slides.heading: Reuse or *extend*
slides.voiceover: Takeaway: include reuses fields across your own tables. Append extends an SAP table like VBAK, without touching it. Always with the Z Z prefix.
slides.spoken: Takeaway: include reuses fields across your own tables. Append extends an SAP table like VBAK, without touching it. Always with the ZZ prefix.

3. Append structure: add your fields to an SAP table like VBAK without a modification

slides.title: READ TABLE can't find *customer 1000*?
slides.voiceover: Your READ TABLE can't find customer one thousand? It's right there in the table.
slides.spoken: Your READ TABLE can't find customer 1000? It's right there in the table.

slides.myth: BINARY SEARCH always makes READ TABLE faster
slides.fact: It only works on a table sorted by that key
slides.voiceover: Myth: BINARY SEARCH always makes READ TABLE faster. Fact: it only works on a table sorted by the key you search.
slides.spoken: Myth: BINARY SEARCH always makes READ TABLE faster. Fact: it only works on a table sorted by the key you search.

slides.label: THE PROBLEM
slides.heading: It throws away the *wrong half*
slides.voiceover: Why? Binary search checks the middle row. One thousand is smaller, so it throws away the bottom half. Unsorted, that's the wrong half. The row is there, and S Y subrc says four.
slides.spoken: Why? Binary search checks the middle row. 1000 is smaller, so it throws away the bottom half. Unsorted, that's the wrong half. The row is there, and sy-subrc says 4.

slides.heading: *SORT* first, then search
slides.code:
SORT lt_kna1 BY kunnr.
READ TABLE lt_kna1 INTO DATA(ls_kna1)
  WITH KEY kunnr = '0000001000'
  BINARY SEARCH.
slides.voiceover: The fix: sort the table by the same field first. Then read it with BINARY SEARCH, using that field in the key.
slides.spoken: The fix: sort the table by the same field first. Then read it with BINARY SEARCH, using that field in the key.

slides.label: THE FIX
slides.heading: Sorted: *two checks*
slides.voiceover: Same search on the sorted table. The middle is three thousand. Keep the left half. Next check: one thousand, found. S Y subrc is zero.
slides.spoken: Same search on the sorted table. The middle is 3000. Keep the left half. Next check: 1000, found. sy-subrc is 0.

slides.label: COMMON MISTAKE
slides.heading: Sorted by the *wrong field*

bad.title: SORT BY name1
bad.sub: then search by kunnr: still misses

good.title: SORT BY kunnr
good.sub: the same field as WITH KEY

slides.voiceover: Common mistake: sorting by name, then searching by customer. Always sort by the same fields you search with.
slides.spoken: Common mistake: sorting by name, then searching by customer. Always sort by the same fields you search with.

slides.label: TAKEAWAY
slides.heading: Sort, then *search*
slides.voiceover: Takeaway: sort by the key, then binary search. Or skip all that and use a sorted table, which searches by its key for you. Customer one thousand, found.
slides.spoken: Takeaway: sort by the key, then binary search. Or skip all that and use a sorted table, which searches by its key for you. Customer 1000, found.

posts.caption:
Your READ TABLE can't find customer 1000? It's right there in the table.

Myth or fact: BINARY SEARCH always makes READ TABLE faster on an internal table.

1. Binary search checks the middle row and throws half the table away
2. On an unsorted table it can throw away the half with your row: sy-subrc 4
3. Fix: SORT the table BY the same field you search with
4. Or use a SORTED table, it searches by its key for you

Comment SORT if this bug ever cost you an afternoon.

slides.title: Will your *table* pass activation?
slides.voiceover: Stop missing these five SE11 table rules. Last time we learned include and append structures. Now, the key rules of tables.
slides.spoken: Stop missing these five SE11 table rules. Last time we learned include and append structures. Now, the key rules of tables.

slides.label: RULE 1
slides.heading: Keys *on top*
slides.voiceover: Why rules? SAP builds the primary key from the top rows. A key field below a normal field isn't allowed. So key fields come first. And in a client table, MANDT is the first key.
slides.spoken: Why rules? SAP builds the primary key from the top rows. A key field below a normal field isn't allowed. So key fields come first. And in a client table, MANDT is the first key.

slides.label: EXAMPLE
slides.heading: *SCARR* follows the rules
slides.title: Table SCARR · Fields
slides.voiceover: Look at SCARR. The client first, then CARRID, both key fields. Then the name and the currency. Each field has a data element.
slides.spoken: Look at SCARR. The client first, then CARRID, both key fields. Then the name and the currency. Each field has a data element.

slides.label: RULES 2-4
slides.heading: Three more *musts*
slides.voiceover: Data elements give every field its labels and F1 help. CURR and QUAN fields need a reference field. Technical settings must be saved before you activate.
slides.spoken: Data elements give every field its labels and F1 help. CURR and QUAN fields need a reference field. Technical settings must be saved before you activate.

slides.label: RULE 5
slides.heading: Activate = *real table*
slides.voiceover: When you activate, SAP creates the real table in the database. Same name, same fields. That's what transparent table means.
slides.spoken: When you activate, SAP creates the real table in the database. Same name, same fields. That's what transparent table means.

slides.label: REMEMBER
slides.heading: Five rules, *one table*
slides.voiceover: Takeaway: keys on top, client first. Data elements on every field, so labels and help come free. Technical settings, then activate.
slides.spoken: Takeaway: keys on top, client first. Data elements on every field, so labels and help come free. Technical settings, then activate.

slides.title: Four *table mistakes* that hurt
slides.voiceover: Stop making these four table mistakes. Last time we learned the key rules of tables. Now, the mistakes and the interview questions.
slides.spoken: Stop making these four table mistakes. Last time we learned the key rules of tables. Now, the mistakes and the interview questions.

slides.label: COMMON MISTAKES
slides.heading: Check these *four*

items.title: No MANDT
items.cons: every client sees the same rows

items.title: Buffering VBAK
items.cons: other servers can read old values

slides.voiceover: Mistake one: no MANDT. Then every client sees the same rows. Two: delivery class A for a settings table. SM30 won't ask for a transport. Three: buffering VBAK. It changes all day, so other servers can read old values. Four: a CURR field without a reference field. Activation fails.
slides.spoken: Mistake one: no MANDT. Then every client sees the same rows. Two: delivery class A for a settings table. SM30 won't ask for a transport. Three: buffering VBAK. It changes all day, so other servers can read old values. Four: a CURR field without a reference field. Activation fails.

slides.heading: Interview *question 1*

messages.text: One table in the database, with the same name and fields as in SE11.

slides.voiceover: Interview question one: what is a transparent table? Answer: one table in the database, with the same name and fields as in SE11.
slides.spoken: Interview question one: what is a transparent table? Answer: one table in the database, with the same name and fields as in SE11.

slides.label: INTERVIEW · Q2
slides.heading: Check table or *value table*?
slides.voiceover: Question two: check table or value table? The value table sits on the domain, like T005 on LAND1. It's only a proposal. The check table is the one the foreign key really checks.
slides.spoken: Question two: check table or value table? The value table sits on the domain, like T005 on LAND1. It's only a proposal. The check table is the one the foreign key really checks.

slides.label: REMEMBER
slides.heading: Check *before* you activate
slides.body: MANDT, delivery class, buffering, reference fields: check all four before every activation.
slides.voiceover: Takeaway: before every activation, check MANDT, the delivery class, buffering and reference fields. Four checks. That's the answer interviewers want.
slides.spoken: Takeaway: before every activation, check MANDT, the delivery class, buffering and reference fields. Four checks. That's the answer interviewers want.
